draft.title: Condensation polymers
card: A condensation polymer forms when monomers with two functional groups join, one link at a time. Each time two monomers link, a small molecule such as water is given off.
made from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid. The amine and carboxyl groups join to form an amide link (-CONH-), as in nylon.
made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid. The hydroxyl and carboxyl groups join to form an ester link (-COO-), as in the polyester PET.
Some monomers carry two different groups, such as an amino acid. Each of these can join to others in a chain and give off water at each link.
draft.remember: Condensation polymers join through two-group monomers, losing a small molecule at every link.

a.q: A diol reacts with a dicarboxylic acid to make a polymer. What are the products?
a.why: Hydroxyl and carboxyl groups form ester links, and water is lost at each link. A polyamide would need an amine group, and a polymer made with no small molecule would be an addition polymer.
a.clue: Name the link made by an alcohol group and an acid group.

b.q: Nylon is made from hexane-1,6-diamine and hexanedioic acid. Which link joins the monomers in the chain?
opts: Carbon to carbon single bond only
b.why: An amine group and a carboxyl group react to form an amide link, and water is given off. An ester link needs a hydroxyl group, which neither monomer has.
b.clue: Look at the names: diamine and acid.

problems.detail: The why says an ester link needs a hydroxyl group 'which neither monomer has', but hexanedioic acid's carboxyl groups (-COOH) contain an -OH. It should say an ester link needs an alcohol (hydroxyl) group, which neither monomer has.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the card's facts check out. One small wording problem: the why for (b) wrongly implies the acid has no hydroxyl, when it should say 'alcohol group'.

flags: Question b, wording: The why says an ester link needs a hydroxyl group 'which neither monomer has', but hexanedioic acid's carboxyl groups (-COOH) contain an -OH. It should say an ester link needs an alcohol (hydroxyl) group, which neither monomer has.
